references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the Lord's Spirit will rest upon the Messiah – [ref:Jes 11:2|Isaiah 11:2] uses the same motif of the Spirit coming upon and remaining on the chosen one, as John testifies.
In [ref:Jes 42:1|Isaiah 42:1], God says, "I have put my Spirit upon him", concerning his chosen servant. This is a direct prophetic background for the Spirit coming down and remaining on Jesus.

[ref:Jes 61:1|Isaiah 61:1] speaks of the Lord's Spirit being upon the anointed one, which Jesus later applies to himself (cf. [ref:Luk 4:18|Luke 4:18]). The coming of the Spirit upon Jesus at his baptism is the fulfillment of this.
[ref:Matt 3:16|Matthew 3:16] is the synoptic parallel where the Spirit descends like a dove and comes upon Jesus at his baptism – the same event that John the Baptist testifies about.
[ref:Mark 1:10|Mark 1:10] describes how Jesus saw the Spirit come down upon him like a dove as he came up out of the water – a parallel account to what John the Baptist testifies about.
[ref:Luk 3:22|Luke 3:22] tells that the Holy Spirit came down upon Jesus in bodily form like a dove – the third synoptic parallel to the baptism event.

In [ref:Joh 1:33-34|John 1:33-34], John the Baptist further explains that it was God who said that the one on whom the Spirit remains is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit – a direct continuation and elaboration of the testimony.
[ref:Joh 3:34|John 3:34] says that God gives the Spirit without measure to the Son, which supports that the Spirit remained upon Jesus as John the Baptist testified.
[ref:Apg 10:38|Acts 10:38] summarizes that God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power – Peter's testimony about the same anointing event that John the Baptist observed.
